title: How AI is revealing the secret lives of animals from hummingbirds to pumas
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 15 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01887-w

Advances in machine learning and other technologies are helping researchers to trace the movements, landmarks and social practices of wildlife.
headline: AI helps scientists track and understand wild animal behavior in nature.
why_it_matters: This research isn't directly about cancer, but the AI techniques being developed to understand animal movements and social patterns could eventually be adapted to track how cancer cells move through the body and interact with each other. Understanding animal behavior also informs conservation efforts that protect ecosystems humans depend on.
key_findings: Machine learning (computer programs that learn patterns from data) can automatically identify and track individual animals from video and camera-trap footage
AI can recognize landmarks and movement patterns, allowing researchers to map where animals go and how they use their environment
These technologies work across many species, from tiny hummingbirds to large predators like pumas, making wildlife monitoring faster and less invasive
Automated analysis reveals social networks and behavioral patterns that would take humans months or years to document by hand
methods_snapshot: Researchers used machine learning algorithms—computer systems trained on thousands of images to recognize animals and their behaviors—combined with camera traps, GPS tracking, and video footage from the field. The AI systems learned to identify individual animals, track their movements over time, and detect patterns in their behavior without human observers needing to be present.

glossary.definition: Computer programs that improve at a task by learning patterns from data, rather than being explicitly programmed with rules.
A step-by-step set of instructions that a computer follows to solve a problem or analyze data.
A motion-activated camera placed in the wild that automatically takes photos or videos when animals pass by.
A type of machine learning system loosely inspired by how brains work, made of interconnected layers that process information.

ml_angle: Artificial intelligence was trained on thousands of animal images to automatically recognize, identify, and track individual animals and their behaviors in videos and photos—a task that would take human researchers years to complete by hand.
limitations: The study focuses on wildlife monitoring rather than cancer research, so its direct medical applications remain unclear. Success of these AI tools depends on having enough high-quality footage and may work better for some species than others.
